answers.question: What should change when this works?
answers.text: Turn one meeting's notes into a clean list of action items, so nobody has to re-read the notes to know who does what by when.

answers.question: Who uses the result, and who approves it?
answers.text: The club's volunteers use the list after each meeting. The coordinator approves it before it is shared. The treasurer only cares that money actions are not lost.

answers.question: How is it done today, and what goes wrong?
answers.text: Today someone re-reads the notes the next day and types a list by hand. Actions get missed, owners are guessed, and two people sometimes do the same job.

answers.question: What is in scope, and what is out?
answers.text: In scope: one meeting's notes as plain text in, one action-item list out. Out of scope: calendars, emails, task tools and more than one meeting at a time.

answers.question: What does the input look like?
answers.text: Plain-text notes of 150 to 400 words, with a date, attendees by first name and discussion paragraphs. The repair café notes in the context pack are a fair sample.

answers.question: What exactly should come out?
answers.text: A Markdown table with one row per action: ID, action starting with a verb, owner, due date and the quoted source sentence.

answers.question: Which quality rules matter, and how serious is breaking each?
answers.text: Every action needs a quoted sentence from the notes; that is major. Owner and due date only from the notes, otherwise 'unassigned' or 'not stated'; major. Nothing missed and no duplicates; major. Actions start with a verb; minor.

answers.question: How will you know it worked?
answers.text: I will know it worked when I can hand the list to the volunteers without opening the notes again.

answers.question: Give two good and two bad rows.
answers.text: Good: 'A1 | Send the revised budget to the team | Priya | Friday 31 Oct | Priya will send the revised budget by Friday.' Good: 'A2 | Collect the spare-parts box | unassigned | not stated | Someone needs to collect the spare-parts box.' Bad: 'A3 | Book the venue | Tom | next week | (no source)', because the owner and date are guessed and nothing is quoted. Bad: 'A4 | the toaster sign-up sheet | Mia | not stated | Mia will print the toaster sign-up sheet.', because it does not start with a verb.

answers.question: What does it touch, and how bad is a mistake?
answers.text: Nothing is written anywhere; the list is just a file I read. If it is wrong I fix it by hand, so it is easy to undo and only affects our team.

answers.question: Where do you want to approve, and what limits?
answers.text: I want to approve every list before it goes out. Keep the factory's default limits.

answers.question: What data is it, and which sources count?
answers.text: All notes are made up for testing. The notes themselves are the only source; nothing from the web.

answers.question: Anything you are unsure about?
answers.text: I don't know yet whether we will want the list as a spreadsheet later.

answers.question: Any words we should define?
answers.text: A commitment is when someone says they will do something. 'Let's discuss it later' is not a commitment.
